edges.title: Céphale et Procris and Lully’s tragédies en musique

works.from: Lully’s tragédies en musique, in a prologue and five acts, at the Académie royale de musique
works.to: Céphale et Procris, tragédie en musique (Paris, 1694)

edges.claim: [[jacquet-de-la-guerre]]’s Céphale et Procris was given by the Académie royale de musique at the Palais-Royal in March 1694 and printed by Christophe Ballard, printer to the king for music. Titon du Tillet described it as a tragedy in five acts with a prologue. Lully had died in 1687. Radio France’s biographical note says she composed it “in the line of” Lully, and the Opéra Royal at Versailles calls its style “distinctly Lullian”.
edges.note: Her dedication to the king names no model. The connection rests on the genre, the theatre and the descriptions by Radio France and the Opéra Royal; no statement by the composer supports it.

edges.title: Corelli and Jacquet de La Guerre’s trio sonatas

works.to: Four trio sonatas, copied by Sébastien de Brossard in 1695

edges.claim: In 1695 [[jacquet-de-la-guerre]] lent Sébastien de Brossard the originals of four trio sonatas “to have them copied”. His manuscript is titled “Sonnatta della signora de la guerre”, with Italian headings for the individual sonatas. Reviewing a recording of the trio sonatas in 2019, Johan van Veen noted that the booklet note names the arrival of Corelli’s trio sonatas, Opp. 1 and 2, in France as a landmark. He heard the influence of Corelli in them and wrote that she was “very much independent of his model”. Of the two solo sonatas copied with them he wrote that she did not follow Corelli’s example slavishly, either in the number of movements or in the order of tempi.
edges.note: No source reports Jacquet de La Guerre or Brossard naming Corelli as the model for these sonatas. The connection rests on the genre, the Italian titles and a reviewer’s comparison.

edges.title: Cantatas on La Motte’s scriptural poems

works.from: Antoine Houdar de La Motte, poems on subjects from Scripture
works.to: Cantates françoises sur des sujets tirez de l’Ecriture, livres 1 and 2 (1708, 1711)

edges.claim: The first book of Cantates françoises sur des sujets tirez de l’Ecriture by [[jacquet-de-la-guerre]], printed by Christophe Ballard in 1708, contains Esther, Le Passage de la mer Rouge, Jacob et Rachel, Jonas, Susanne et les vieillards and Judith. The Journal des sçavans of 7 January 1709 named Houdar de La Motte as the author of the words. The Philidor catalogue lists him as the poet of all twelve cantatas in the two books, which Cessac dates to 1708 and 1711.

edges.title: Titon du Tillet’s Parnasse françois entry, 1732

works.to: Her life and works; the medal inscribed “Aux grands Musiciens j’ay disputé le prix”

edges.claim: Titon du Tillet gave [[jacquet-de-la-guerre]] a long entry in Le Parnasse françois of 1732. He recounted her years at court under Madame de Montespan, her marriage, her improvising and her works, and wrote that “never has anyone of her sex had such great talents as she for composing music”. The Philidor catalogue reports that her portrait appears there as a medallion with the legend “Aux grands Musiciens j’ay disputé le prix”, and a Bibliothèque nationale print by L. Crépy dated 1729 shows the medal with that legend.

sources.title: Titon du Tillet, Le Parnasse françois (Paris, 1732), entry CCXLIX, pp. 635–636
